verdicts.evidence:
I used a fresh local copy (API 8401, site 4401, database candela_v8401), built by /home/user/pt3/verify/v8401_setup.js. It has one Lightkeeper and five approved investigators, the fifth being 'Pontius Aganus'. /home/user/pt3/verify/v8401_ghost.js then tried every server path that could take an approved investigator off a campaign:
- POST /campaign/reject/5 as the Lightkeeper: 400 'Character is not in pending status or does not exist'.
- POST /campaign/withdraw/5 as the owner: 409 'This request is no longer waiting.'
- DELETE /api/investigators/5 as the owner: 409 'An investigator in a campaign cannot be deleted.'
- SQL afterwards: still status active, campaign 1.
I then listed every button on the Lightkeeper's desk at 1440x900 (out_8401/g01_desk.png) and on Pontius's open sheet (g02_sheet.png). Nothing reads release, remove, kick, dismiss, leave, unapprove or reject. The only bulk control is RETIRE CAMPAIGN. The Finalize slip reads '5 in the circle (up to 5)', so the ghost takes the last seat.
v8401_reports.js then sealed the circle over the API. SQL gives stitch, refresh and train = 6 each. The Roster's circle file (r08_roster_ledger.png) shows 'STITCH 6 · max 6', 'REFRESH 6 · max 6', 'TRAIN 6 · max 6' and 'Reports Open · 4 of 5 filed'. With four real players the rulebook (p. 41, p. 62) gives 5 each.
With four of five reports filed, each with a key, the tally reads 'Keys: some investigators (4 of 5) +2'. The 'every investigator' 4 cannot be reached while the ghost stays (r04_tally.png).
This is not in #16 and not among the open issues: #16 covers retire and restore only, and #41 and #47 are different. FAQ.md:163-165 only describes approving and rejecting pending requests, and neither FAQ nor DESIGN says an approval is final.
verdicts.root_cause:
No code path lets go of an active, living investigator except retiring or deleting the whole campaign:
- backend/engine.py:112-121 reject_investigator only acts when character.status == "pending". The route at backend/vtt/routers/campaigns.py:222-255 maps anything else to 400.
- backend/vtt/routers/campaigns.py:328-342 withdraw_request refuses non-pending with 409.
- backend/vtt/deletion.py:117-127 delete_character refuses ROSTER_STATUSES with 409.
- The only release is retire_campaign (campaigns.py:257-292) and delete_campaign.
Every count therefore keeps counting the ghost:
- resource_pool (backend/vtt/circle_queries.py:26-39) counts every active living character, which gives 1+5=6.
- tallyReports (frontend/src/game/illumination.js:17-23) uses all living investigators as the member count.
- The formation papers and the Finalize slip count all active members.
The frontend has Approve and two-press Reject only for pending requests (DESIGN.md:380), and nothing for an approved one.
verdicts.fix:
Needs a product decision on what a release does after the seal: votes, relationships, a filed report, and whether resources are recomputed or clamped.
Smallest correct change:
- Backend: add POST /campaign/release/{character_id} (GM of the campaign only) in backend/vtt/routers/campaigns.py, or widen engine.reject_investigator. It should accept an active, not-dead character and do for that one character what retire_campaign does at campaigns.py:274-280: status = 'unaffiliated', campaign_id = None, ink_color = '', end_assignment_for(c).
- Also remove its pending circle votes, its relationship proposals and its entry in backstory_answers.reports.
- After the seal, clamp the circle's stitch, refresh and train to the new resource_pool(circle). Otherwise only later refills follow the smaller pool.
- Broadcast investigator_rejected (or a new investigator_released) to its character channel. Call _announce_members_changed and log 'The Lightkeeper released <name>.'
- Frontend: on the Lightkeeper's copy of an approved sheet, add a two-press 'Release' using the same pattern as the waiting-request strip's Reject (gm desk sheet strip, DESIGN.md:380 pattern). Its second-press text should say the investigator goes back to its player.
- Alternative, smaller but weaker fix: give Approve a second-press warning that approval is final.

refute.reasoning:
The core claim holds, and I checked it in the code myself; no repro was needed. engine.reject_investigator (backend/engine.py:112-121) only works on a 'pending' character. withdraw (campaigns.py:328-342) only works on pending. delete_character refuses a character that is on a roster. Every other place that sets status to 'unaffiliated' or 'retired' is one of these: retire_campaign (campaigns.py:274-276), the restore/delete path (campaigns.py:452, deletion.py:165), the release of still-pending characters at finalize (circles.py:284), or the retiring of a dead predecessor at approval (engine.py:97). None of them lets the Lightkeeper release one approved, living investigator. resource_pool (circle_queries.py:26-39) counts every active, living member, and tallyReports (illumination.js) counts every living investigator as a member. So the ghost inflates the pool to 6 and makes the +4 key bonus unreachable.

The documents do not excuse it. FAQ.md:163-165 and DESIGN.md:380 cover only pending requests, and nothing calls approval final. QUIRKS.md has no entry for it. #16 covers whole-campaign retire and restore only, and no open issue (#41, #47 or the #45 checklist) matches it. The rulebook (p. 41/62) counts the players at the table, so 5 is right for four players. This was a real player in the real playtest, not a setup the harness built.

The case against holds only on severity, which is overstated in two ways.
(1) The 5-seat cap is not enforced. "Up to 5" is just hint text in FinalizeRosterSlip.jsx:68. Neither join nor approve has a member limit, so the ghost does not actually block a fifth real player. The claim that it "takes the last seat" should be cut.
(2) The Lightkeeper can correct the worst numbers by hand. Stitch, Refresh and Train are editable by the Lightkeeper (FAQ.md:268). Illumination can be edited directly too (FAQ.md:222), so the missing +2 of the key bonus can be added by hand. The ghost also does not block finalizing: the seal goes through with votes missing.

What still has no workaround: the ghost stays in voter and relationship lists, gets a report card, and sets every refill back to 6 so it needs re-editing. The only full fix is retiring the whole campaign. That makes this a real bug at medium severity, not high.

The proposed fix is sound: a Lightkeeper-only release endpoint, plus clean-up of votes, proposals and reports, a clamp of the resources, a two-press Release on the approved sheet, and a broadcast and log line. Two adjustments:
- Drop the seat-cap rationale.
- When the reports are tallied, base the member count on the same set of members that resource_pool uses, so the two counts cannot drift apart.

verdicts.evidence: I ran a fresh local copy (API on 8402, site on 4402, database candela_v8402) and forged two investigators with Nerve at its legal 0 start: a Professor with Well-Read and Nerve 0/0, and an Occultist with Nerve 0/0. The database row is nerve_max=0, nerve_current=0. GET /api/investigators/<id> returns nerve_current 0 and nerve_max 1, both for the player and for the Lightkeeper looking at a pending applicant (the Pontius case, 'lk pending 0/1'). On the tablet (820x1180, touch) the dossier's screen-reader text is 'Nerve: 0 of 1 available.' and it draws one solid empty pip, unlike the dotted pips beyond the maximum (out_8402/drive_00_desk.png, drive_01_after_tap.png). The desktop at 1920x1080 shows the same pip (wr_02_after.png). Tapping the live 'Set Nerve available to 1' button sends update_drive {pool:nerve,value:1}, and the server answers action_rejected 422 'A drive is a whole number from 0 to its maximum.' I then spent a circle Refresh over the player's socket: the log said 'drives & resistances restored', the database still has Nerve 0/0, and the sheet still reads 'Nerve: 0 of 1 available.' with the empty pip (drive_02_after_refresh.png). This is not intended behaviour: the creator and forge allow a drive of 0 (creation.py:170, test_investigators.py:122), handle_update_drive and Refresh treat the maximum as 0, and nothing in FAQ.md, DESIGN.md, QUIRKS.md or the tests pins the 'or 1'. It is not in issues.md and is not a #16 item. I rated it medium rather than high: the number is wrong and a control is offered that the server refuses, but no rule is misapplied and the server stays correct.
verdicts.root_cause: backend/vtt/serializers.py:60, 63 and 66 send `getattr(char, "nerve_max", 1) or 1` (the same for cunning_max and intuition_max), so a stored maximum of 0 goes out as 1. The frontend repeats the fallback in frontend/src/components/pc/InvestigatorDossier.jsx:982 (`const maxDrive = character[`${cat.driveKey}_max`] || 1;`, which draws the pips and the 'of N' text and makes pip 0 a live refill button) and at :579 in handleSpendDrive. Smaller knock-ons of the inflated value: CircleView.jsx:399 would label an advancement drive pick 'nerve (1 ...)', and gameStore.js:242 uses `|| 1`, which is harmless because floor(1/3) is 0.
verdicts.fix: In serializers.py:60, 63 and 66 use `getattr(char, "<drive>_max", 0) or 0`. In InvestigatorDossier.jsx:579 and :982 use `?? 0` (or `|| 0`) instead of `|| 1`; with a maximum of 0 every pip is dotted, nothing is offered, and value > 0 is refused locally. Optionally print 'none' for a 0-maximum drive, as the Resistance row already does. For consistency also change gameStore.js:242 to `|| 0`. No product decision is needed. Add a serializer test that a 0 maximum round-trips as 0.

verdicts.evidence: Same fresh local copy, desktop 1920x1080. A Professor with Well-Read and Intuition 4/4 pressed 'Spend one more Intuition for +1d' (4 to 3) and rolled Focus (gilded, rating 2). The dice were gilded 3, 2 and 5, and I kept the gilded die with Enter ('Keep the gilded 3: Failure, 1 Intuition back'). The server sent the activity_log 'Ada Prof rolled read — 3 · Failure (...kept the gilded 3). [gilded — intuition Drive refreshed] [Well-Read — 1 Intuition refunded]', and the desk shows '(Gilded die kept: 1 Intuition refreshed) (Well-Read: 1 Intuition back)'. character_update and the database both end at Intuition 4/4: one point was spent and one came back, but the log claims two. The slip says only '1 Intuition back' (out_8402/wr_02_after.png). The rules effect is right: FAQ.md:241/244 makes both automatic, and a drive cannot pass its maximum. Only the log line overstates. The code's own rule agrees that this is a defect: the _refresh_drive docstring (rolls.py:116-117) says 'so the log never says a point came back that did not', and the gilded line follows that rule while the Well-Read line does not. Not in issues.md or the #45 checklist, and not a #16 item.
verdicts.root_cause: backend/vtt/ws/handlers/rolls.py:588-592 (handle_resolve_gilded) sets `character.intuition_current = min(character.intuition_max or 3, (character.intuition_current or 0) + spent)` and then always appends `[Well-Read — {spent} Intuition refunded]` and sets changed=True, without checking how much the cap let through. The same pattern is in the no-choice roll path at rolls.py:525-529 (reached after an auto gilded refresh, for example when every die is gilded).
verdicts.fix: In both places, measure what actually came back: `before = character.intuition_current or 0; character.intuition_current = min(character.intuition_max or 0, before + spent); back = character.intuition_current - before`. Log `[Well-Read — {back} Intuition refunded]` and mark the sheet changed only when back > 0 (or say the refund was capped, if the owner prefers that wording). This also covers a partial cap, such as a 2-point spend where only 1 can come back. No change to the rules.

refute.reasoning:
I tried five ways to knock this down, and none worked.

1. **Intended behaviour or rulebook.** The rules effect is right. FAQ.md:241 and FAQ.md:244 make Well-Read and the gilded refresh both automatic, and a drive cannot go past its maximum, so ending at 4/4 is correct. The fault is only the log text. The code's own rule says so: the `_refresh_drive` docstring (rolls.py:116-117) says "so the log never says a point came back that did not". The gilded line follows that rule. The Well-Read line at rolls.py:588-591 does not: it caps the value with `min()`, then always adds `[Well-Read — {spent} Intuition refunded]` and sets `changed=True`.

2. **Pinned by a test or listed as a quirk.** No. The two tests that cover this are `test_well_read_refunds_on_a_kept_die_of_three_or_less` (keeps a regular die, Intuition 4/6) and `test_well_read_refunds_intuition_on_failure` (3/3, spend 1, refund 1). Neither reaches the cap. QUIRKS.md has nothing on Well-Read.

3. **Duplicate or #16 item.** No. issues.md has nothing on gilded, refresh, Well-Read or log overstatement, including the #45 checklist, and none of the #16 items applies.

4. **Unrealistic setup or harness artifact.** No. It only needs a Scholar with Well-Read and full Intuition who spends 1 Intuition on a gilded Intuition action, then keeps the gilded die on a failure. The playtest hit this in ordinary play (F052), and the verifier reproduced it locally, with character_update and the database both ending at 4/4.

5. **Root cause.** It cannot happen without the gilded refresh. A spend takes `spent` off the drive and Well-Read puts the same amount back, so the cap only matters when the gilded refresh has already put a point back first. That means the cluster is fully described by the resolve_gilded path, plus the no-choice path after `auto_gilded_refresh` (rolls.py:520-529), as the verifier says.

**Severity.** Low is right: no game state is wrong, and only the log line overstates. One wording point: the triage entry has kind "rules", but the rules are applied correctly. It is a log-accuracy defect, which the entry's own notes admit.

**Fix.** Measuring `before` and `after` and logging the real amount, only when it is above 0, is right and also covers a partial cap. One small change: keep the existing fallback for a missing maximum (`intuition_max or 3`) rather than changing it to `or 0`. That avoids a quiet change in behaviour, though the database values are never null in practice. Separately, the no-choice path calls `min(getattr(character, "intuition_max", 3), ...)` with no `or` guard, so a null maximum would raise there. That is not part of this finding.

verdicts.evidence:
I ran this on a fresh local copy (API 8403, site 4403, database candela_v8403): Lightkeeper desk at 1440x900, Notebook > Sketch, Text tool, driven with real mouse clicks and keyboard typing (scripts /home/user/pt3/verify/v8403_sketch*.js, shots in /home/user/pt3/verify/out_8403/). The Text button stayed pressed the whole time (aria-pressed=Text after every step), so the triage's 'tool falls to Select' is wrong. Labels are still lost, in two ways a real mouse also hits.
(A) The finding's flow: click, type 'Wick Lane / loft', Enter (adds a newline inside the label), click elsewhere, type 'slipway (choir loudest)', click, type 'bell rope'. The click elsewhere only closed the first label; no editor opened, and the typed letters went nowhere. Only 2 of 3 labels exist (s_A.png). Typing letter by letter after such a click left the tool on Text (s_D run).
(C) The 'Escape to finish' route: Escape, then one click for the next label. That click reopened the PREVIOUS label (still selected) and the typing replaced its text. After three labels only 'bell rope' remains, at the first label's spot (s_C.png). Pressing 'e' after Escape switched the tool to Eraser (v8403_sketch3.js), which matches the Eraser seen in beta shot 091.
(B) Clicking twice per label (once to close, once to start) keeps every label (s_B.png).
I also injected a capture-phase pointerdown on .sketch-canvas that blurs the open label first. With it, all 5 of the playtest's labels were made with one click each (s_fix_sim.png).
This contradicts DESIGN.md 'Sketch sheet': 'A tool stays in hand ... a box, a line or a word never turns it back into select, so the next stroke draws again'. It is not in issues.md (#21 and #44 are different) and not a #16 item. The ink recolouring the last label is by design (SketchPad applyStyle comment) and is not part of this verdict.
verdicts.root_cause:
frontend/src/components/shared/sketch/SketchPad.jsx:154/179/187 locks every tool, Text included. Excalidraw 0.18 was not written for a locked Text tool, and the sheet does not adapt:
(1) In Excalidraw's handleTextOnPointerDown (node_modules/@excalidraw/excalidraw/dist/dev/index.js:27985-27988), a click while a label is open only finishes it, 'irrespective of locked'. So the next click never starts a label, and keys typed then are lost or used as shortcuts.
(2) An Escape (keyboard) submit selects the finished text (index.js:30755-30767). startTextEditing (index.js:26619-26623) then reuses the one selected text element on the next Text click, because clearSelectionIfNotUsingSelection's setState has not landed yet. The next label overwrites the last one.
verdicts.fix:
Two small changes in SketchPad.jsx.
(a) On the canvas wrapper (line 334), add a capture-phase handler that finishes an open label before Excalidraw sees the click, so that same click starts the next label: onPointerDownCapture={(e) => { if (lastTool.current !== 'text') return; const ed = wrapRef.current?.querySelector('textarea.excalidraw-wysiwyg'); if (ed && e.target !== ed) ed.blur(); }}. I checked this in the browser: 5 of 5 labels.
(b) In onChange (around line 175), when now === 'text' and !appState.editingTextElement and any selectedElementIds are set, clear the selection with api.updateScene({ appState: { selectedElementIds: {} } }). Then after Escape the next click makes a new label and does not reopen the old one. This is what pressing the T button already does through setActiveTool.
Optional: say in DESIGN.md that Enter adds a line inside a label and a click elsewhere starts the next one.

verdicts.root_cause:
1) frontend/src/components/shared/NotebookView.jsx:231 is setCount(Math.max(3, fits)). It forces at least 3 contents lines per page even when only 1 fits, so the rest hide in the list's own overflow-y-auto scroll and the page count understates them.
2) NotebookView.jsx:1191: a contents line only calls setCurrentSpread(entrySpread(entry)) and never brings the entry into view. After posting an entry, lines 694-705 already turn the page and scroll the new card into view, but the contents does not do this.
verdicts.fix:
1) NotebookView.jsx:231: change to setCount(Math.max(1, fits)), so each contents page holds only the lines that fit and the arrows page through the rest.
2) Move the requestAnimationFrame / scrollIntoView / focus block from handleSubmitEntry (lines 697-705) into a showEntry(id) helper. Call it from the contents button: onClick={() => { setCurrentSpread(entrySpread(entry)); showEntry(entry.id); }}. Use block 'start' so the entry's title sits at the top of its page scroller.
Keep three entries to a page, as DESIGN.md asks.

verdicts.evidence:
Local copy (API 8404, site 4404, fresh DB), sealed campaign with reports_open=true, Iris Vane (Criminal) at 1920x1080 with a mouse. Script: /home/user/pt3/verify/v8404_keys.js. Shots: /home/user/pt3/verify/out_8404/keys_01_pinned.png, keys_03_hover_moved.png, keys_06_phone_after_tap.png.

With the slip closed, the three key boxes are at y 342, 366 and 390 (x 931). After a click on the 'Criminal Illumination Keys' term, the slip is at x924 y331, 288x85, and covers all three boxes and their labels. elementFromPoint at every box centre and every label text returns the tooltip. Two real mouse clicks at the first box's position did nothing: the box stayed unchecked and the slip stayed pinned.

Hover alone (no click) does the same. Pointing at the heading and moving down to the first box goes onto the slip, which keeps it open (onPointerEnter on the slip). It was still covering the boxes 800 ms after the click, and the box was not ticked.

Phone 390x844 with touch: tapping the 'i' pins the slip over the first two boxes. A tap on the first box lands on the slip, changes nothing and does not close it.

A person cannot see the boxes under the opaque slip, so they would probably click elsewhere rather than blind on the box. That way out works, but the heading's help hides exactly the list it explains, and moving the pointer down onto the list keeps it hidden.

This is a new place for an already-filed pattern: the #45 checklist item 'At 1366x768 the what-a-reroll-throws i slip covers Burn and reroll' is the same kind of problem. It is not a #16 item: help on demand is kept, and the issue is only where the slip lies.
verdicts.root_cause:
frontend/src/components/pc/CircleView.jsx:763. This InfoTerm takes the default slipClassName from frontend/src/components/shared/ActionInfo.jsx:105 ('left-0 top-full mt-1 w-[min(18rem,...)]'), so the slip lies directly under the heading, on top of the key list (lines 765-777). InfoTerm's own comment (ActionInfo.jsx:84-85) says callers should lay the slip beside their column, not under the term, and this caller does not.

Separately, a press on the slip counts as inside the term (onDown checks ref.contains, ActionInfo.jsx:142), so it never unpins. Hovering the slip also cancels the leave timer (onEnterSlip, line 157), which keeps it up while the pointer is over the boxes.
verdicts.fix: At CircleView.jsx:763, pass a slipClassName that keeps the slip off the list: open it above the heading (for example slipClassName="left-0 bottom-full mb-1 w-[min(18rem,calc(100vw-2.5rem))]"), which covers only the non-interactive intro paragraph. What the tablet showed:

The playtest Lightkeeper did open spending mid-assignment (table.md line 49) and again after End Assignment (line 74). Dev's Train in F130 was bought after End and survives, so in that case only the wording is wrong.

Neither FAQ.md nor DESIGN.md settles which wording is right. FAQ says 'each player has two per assignment', while the Circle page says 'between assignments'. The rulebook p. 41 (Train for the next assignment) sides with the card. The 'Lightkeeper cannot spend for a player' part of F086 is an idea, not a defect.
verdicts.root_cause:
There are two models of when spends happen, and the code mixes them.

The server counts spends and Train dice per assignment and wipes both at End Assignment: backend/vtt/assignment.py:76-79 (end_assignment_for sets resources_spent_assignment=0, train_bonus=False, train_dice=0), called from backend/vtt/ws/handlers/gm.py:370-371. The Lightkeeper may open spending at any time (gm.py:265), and End Assignment does not close it.

The wording disagrees:
- frontend/src/components/pc/CircleView.jsx:52 and frontend/src/game/circleResources.js:7 say 'next assignment'.
- backend/vtt/ws/handlers/circle.py:102 (log) and frontend/src/game/rollMods.js:140-146 (chip) say 'this assignment'.
- frontend/src/game/circleResources.js:23-24 says 'between assignments'.
- frontend/src/components/gm/GMCharacterSheet.jsx:37 says 'Circle spends this assignment'.

The effect: a Train bought while an assignment is open can be used at once ('this assignment'), but if it is not used before End Assignment it is silently destroyed, even though the card promises it for the next assignment.
verdicts.fix:
Needs a product decision on when spends happen.

Smallest change that matches rulebook p. 41 and the card:
- Stop End Assignment from clearing Train dice: drop the train_bonus/train_dice lines at assignment.py:78-79, so a bought die lasts until a roll uses it.
- Make the log say the same thing as the card: circle.py:102 becomes 'a Train d6 for a roll of their choice, kept until used' (or '... in the next assignment').
- rollMods.js:146 becomes 'Train (+1d on this roll; n Train die/dice banked)'.
- GMCharacterSheet.jsx:37 becomes 'Circle spends' plus the counter, or uses circleResources.js's 'between assignments' wording, so every place says one thing.

A test pins End Assignment clearing Train dice (QUIRKS.md line 184 and the end-assignment tests), so that test changes with the decision.

Alternative, if spends should only happen between assignments: have gm_end_assignment open spending and have Dispatch lock it, so no spend falls inside an assignment.

verdicts.evidence:
I ran a fresh local copy (API 8405, site 4405, database candela_v8405) and built a sealed table over the API: one player, pav52yqm, with Iris Vane in The Saltmere Chapter. Script: /home/user/pt3/verify/v8405_logout.js, laptop 1440x900.
(A) I signed in through the slip and reached the hub (out_8405/v8405_a1_hub.png). Then I changed the password from a second login token over the API (POST /api/auth/me/password, which is what the account page on another device sends). Pressing Case Ledger got 401s on GET /api/users/3/characters, /campaigns and /retired-campaigns. The page dropped to the CHAPTER ADMISSION slip with an empty username. No [role=status], [role=alert] or aria-live region held any text (v8405_a2_after_ledger.png, v8405_a3_after_play.png).
(B) I signed in again with the new password and opened Iris Vane's desk (v8405_b1_desk.png). I changed the password from 'another device' again. The server closed the socket with 4401 and the desk went straight to the same empty sign-in slip, with no word of why (v8405_b2_after_4401.png). Status regions were empty and the body text was only the admission form.
I looked at all screenshots. The part about Create account is a harness artifact: locally, Create account through the slip lands on the chapter hub signed in (v8405_j0_signup_wide.png). On beta the 401 came from the sandbox proxy only.
Not a #16 item and not in issues.md. AUTH.md line 141 describes the mechanism: a 401 logs out and goes back to the login screen. It sets no rule that this must happen silently. The site already shows a notice for a related case: a password reset puts a 'Password set' stamp on the slip (LoginScreen.jsx ~637).
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/utils/api.js:23 calls onUnauthorized() on any 401 to a request that carried a token. frontend/src/store/gameStore.js:2336 wires that to logout(), and gameStore.js:708 does the same for a WebSocket 4401 close. logout() (gameStore.js:526) clears accessSession and sets stage 'LOGIN' but keeps no reason. So LoginScreen.jsx renders the plain slip with no notice and no username filled in.
verdicts.fix: Add a store flag such as sessionEnded (not persisted) and an endSession() action: it runs logout() and then sets { sessionEnded: true }, and does nothing if there is no accessSession, so three parallel 401s show the notice once. Use endSession in configureApiAuth's onUnauthorized (gameStore.js:2336) and in the 4401 branch (gameStore.js:708). Leave the deliberate logout() calls alone: Sign out, reset done, undo email. In LoginScreen.jsx, at the sign-in slip, render the same kind of role=status block as afterReset: 'Your session ended (the password may have changed on another device). Please sign in again.' Optionally fill in the last username. Clear the flag on a successful sign-in (setAccessSession) or when the user switches to Create account. Small: about 15 lines across gameStore.js and LoginScreen.jsx. The exact wording is a product choice.

verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/AppRouter.jsx:191 calls setHubNotice(`${name} asked to join. The hub will say when the Lightkeeper answers.`). It is third person, has no subject the player recognises as themselves, and leaves out the campaign. The campaign name is available at that point: fetchUserData has just run (line 187), and the store's characters carry .campaign, which usePendingApprovalWatch.js:23 already uses.
verdicts.fix: In AppRouter.jsx handleForge, after the await fetchUserData(...) at line 187, look up the campaign: const campaign = useGameStore.getState().characters.find(c => c.id === savedCharacter?.id)?.campaign. Then set the notice to `You asked to join ${campaign || 'the campaign'} with ${name}. The hub will say when the Lightkeeper answers.` One line, wording only. The exact sentence is the owner's to pick.
